meaning: Factual source tables and source-only conversions; no Engine prediction or parameter qualification.

sources.locators: Table 1 and 2 p.314; procedure p.313; activity derivation pp.315-318
sources.citation: R. A. Robinson and V. E. Bower, Properties of Aqueous Mixtures of Pure Salts. Thermodynamics of the Ternary System: Water-Sodium Chloride-Calcium Chloride at 25 C, Journal of Research of the National Bureau of Standards A 70A (1966), 313-318.

sources.locators: Table 1 p.18; reference method p.14; dispersion pp.19,21; symbols p.24

transcription: Printed decimal tokens and source locators are preserved. Source blank cells are not filled, except explicitly marked structural pure-salt zeros. Shared reference values copied from table headers retain their source groups.
conditions: 298.15 K (25 C); isopiestic papers do not establish a complete pressure correction. Pressure is not a measured domain here.

measurement_roles.robinson-bower-1966: Table 1 is isopiestic solution composition and ratio data. Table 2 gives NaCl reference anchors at mean reference molalities. Converted Phi uses actual Table 1 reference molality, a piecewise-linear Table 2 reference, and the explicit NaCl/CaCl2 molalities. Pure CaCl2 endpoints and Table 2 anchors are reference checks.
measurement_roles.rard-miller-1987: Tables I-II contain total formula-salt molality and ionic-strength fractions, referenced to each printed NaCl or CaCl2 solution. Source Eq.4 converts the reference particle molality times Phi to mixture Phi. Table III is a separate binary MgCl2 reference check. The source-zero-weight mixture is retained and marked.
measurement_roles.dinane-mounir-2003: Table 1 water activities are primary observations. Ionic strength and printed fraction labels are derived. Growth ratios and assigned reference activities are diagnostic inputs to the original method; no calibration curve or row-specific reference molality is supplied.

robinson-bower-1966.meaning: No numerical per-row coefficient/activity uncertainty is supplied. Printed ratio-fit differences are not uncertainty. Five molality/ratio/fraction inconsistencies remain in the source tokens.

rard-miller-1987.meaning: Stock and reference contributions are shared systematic effects. The five low-concentration equilibrations are not identified cell by cell. Scatter about a smooth curve is not an independent pointwise sigma. The source says 224 points below I=6.16, while its printed cells reconstruct 223.

dinane-mounir-2003.meaning: Pages 19 and 21 describe fit/model dispersions, while the page 24 symbols call them measured-quantity uncertainties. Their scope is unresolved; they supply neither independent row weights nor a confidence claim.

mixing_basis: Formula-salt molality is mol/kg water. For NaCl plus MCl2, I=m_N+3 m_D, q=2 m_N+3 m_D. Robinson particle fraction is 3 m_Ca/q; Rard/Dinane NaCl ionic-strength fraction is m_N/I. These fractions differ.

conversions.Rard: m_N=3 y m_T/(1+2y); m_Mg=(1-y)m_T/(1+2y); Phi=nu_ref*m_ref*Phi_ref/q, nu_ref=2 for NaCl and 3 for CaCl2. Converted aw=exp(-M_w*q*Phi) is the same observation, not another measurement.
conversions.Robinson: Phi=(2 M_B/q)*Phi_NaCl(M_B). Piecewise-linear interpolation of Table 2 mean-M_B anchors, using the first segment for the short extension to M_B=0.5339. The converted file retains local-three-anchor quadratic and printed-R alternatives. The maximum linear/quadratic induced Phi change is 0.00011467728984893838; this is a reconstruction sensitivity estimate, not a rigorous error bound or measurement uncertainty.
conversions.Dinane: No derived Phi is added to the source water-activity table. Explicit molalities determine the composition; printed y=0.33/0.50/0.67 are labels.
